solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Middle of slit appearing in clear blind (9)

indicators.note: the middle letters make an appearance inside the other word, so one sits within the other

blocks.note: clear = obvious; it opens around the inserted letters
the two central letters of sLIt

annotation.surface: Someone peers through a gap in a see-through window blind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blind' looks like the window fitting the surface describes; it is the adjective, as in blind to danger.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the figurative sense: someone blind to a risk is unaware of it.

entries.clue: Love unchanged for band formed in the 1990s (5)

blocks.note: love = nil = O, from tennis scoring
as is = unchanged, left as it was

annotation.surface: A pop fan insists their love for a nineties band has never wavered.
annotation.walkthrough: The Gallagher brothers' Manchester group, formed in 1991, were the leading Britpop band.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Britpop group led by Liam and Noel Gallagher started in Manchester in 1991.

entries.clue: Lure fish to surface downwind (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up to the surface means reading from the bottom upward

blocks.note: to draw someone in is to lure them
the eel is the crossword's favourite fish

annotation.surface: An angler tempts fish upward, drifting with the wind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surface' reads as the water's surface in the fishing picture; in a down clue it means come up, i.e. reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the lee side is the side sheltered from, and so facing away from, the wind.

entries.clue: Shot movie with a cadre — and this? (5,6)

annotation.definition: Shot movie with a cadre — and this?

indicators.note: shot = ruined, broken up, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A film crew shot their movie with a small team, and asks what they used.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight, it asks what else you shot the movie with. 'Shot' first reads as filmed, then as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks what equipment the crew filmed with, and the device answers it.

entries.clue: What cuts across if you become inflexible (6)

indicators.note: the answer is what cuts through the word boundaries, spanning several words

annotation.surface: A question about what happens to a person who grows set in their ways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Across' seems to be about the grid, but it is simply part of the text concealing the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: literally turning to bone, and so growing rigid in habits or opinions.

entries.clue: Get rid of career event (4,4)

blocks.note: to sack someone is to get rid of them
career as a verb = rush headlong

annotation.surface: Someone is dismissed in a single career-ending episode.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' reads as a job, which suits 'get rid of'; here it is the verb, to hurtle along.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a school sports-day event where children hop along inside sacks.

entries.clue: With periodical exceptions, admen pitch intensity (5)

indicators.note: letters are excepted, left out, at regular periods, keeping every other one

blocks.note: aDmEn PiTcH, keeping the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

annotation.surface: Advertising people make their sales pitch with fervour, give or take a lapse or two.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests an advertising sales pitch; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as of feeling or colour: great depth of emotion is great intensity.

entries.clue: God originally ignored Babel (3)

indicators.note: what comes originally, the first letter, is ignored and left off

blocks.note: Odin is the chief Norse god

annotation.surface: A god pays no heed to the tower of Babel, as in the Bible story.
annotation.walkthrough: Babel is best known as the Biblical tower, but here it is simply noisy confusion.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a babel is a confused noise of many voices, taking its name from the tower.

entries.clue: Drop goodness, in part (7)

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: pt is the standard abbreviation for part
an old British exclamation of surprise, from 'Lord love me', used like 'goodness!'

annotation.surface: Someone lets goodness fall away, but only partly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' looks like virtue; it is the exclamation, and the British equivalent is a dated Cockney one.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as a verb: prices or stones fall sharply.

entries.clue: Richer hay deployed to make pyramid? (9)

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A farmer spreads out the best hay to build a haystack in a pyramid shape.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a pyramid is one shape an organisation takes, with few at the top and many below.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a ranked organisation, narrowing to one at the top, is often drawn as a pyramid.

entries.clue: Objects primarily seen in dashes? (7)

indicators.note: what comes primarily, first of all, is the opening letter
the letter shows up inside the other word

annotation.surface: A riddle about which objects you mainly see on dashes.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'dashes' as dashboards and the whole clue is the definition: these dials are what you mainly see on a car's dash.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: speedometers, informally shortened, are the main objects on a dashboard.

entries.clue: Obsess about problem splitting United (7)

indicators.note: the problem goes into the middle of United, dividing it

blocks.note: people who are united are as one
a sum is an arithmetic problem

annotation.surface: Someone fixates on a rift within Manchester United.
annotation.walkthrough: Capitalised United looks like a football club; it is just 'as one'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a passion that eats you up, as in 'consumed by jealousy', obsesses you.

entries.clue: Mark discussed pop music (3)

indicators.note: a word said in discussion is spoken, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound; say it with a British accent that drops the r

annotation.surface: Someone named Mark talks about pop music.
annotation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name. The sound match works only in accents that drop the final r.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Jamaican genre, forerunner of reggae, is a kind of popular music.

entries.clue: Steer towards capital of curtailed fighting — it’s near the end of the list? (6,5)

annotation.definition: it’s near the end of the list?

indicators.note: the tail, last letter, is cut off

blocks.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

annotation.surface: A general steers toward the capital as a cut-short war winds down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital of' looks like a phrase, but the break falls between them: capital is DC, and 'of' is shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the serial comma before 'and' comes just ahead of the final list item, as in red, white, and blue.

entries.clue: 10 data manipulated with confusing cruelty (3-3-5)

indicators.note: the letters are handled and moved around

annotation.surface: Consumer data is misused in a baffling, heartless way.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies letters: the answer to 10 across joins DATA to make the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a game in which a predator toys with its victim, keeping it confused before the kill.

entries.clue: Crazy promotion following introduction of Microsoft Excel (6)

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so take the opening letter
the rest comes after that first letter

blocks.note: to cap is to top or outdo, i.e. excel

annotation.surface: A wild marketing campaign launches after Microsoft Excel is introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: Microsoft Excel looks like the spreadsheet; the two words split, one giving M and the other a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: recklessly wild and eccentric.

entries.clue: Wise partner increasingly snubbed bank (9)

indicators.note: a snub nose is short, so the word's end is cut off

blocks.note: camber is the bank of a road; lose its last letter

annotation.surface: A sensible partner gets more and more short with the bank.
annotation.walkthrough: Wise looks like an adjective; it is Ernie Wise, half of a much-loved British comedy double act.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: Eric, the other half of the comedy duo with Ernie Wise.

entries.clue: Rejected civil engineer still delighted (8)

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters run the other way

annotation.surface: A civil engineer turned down for a job is still somehow thrilled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'even so' after rejection; it means motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, somewhat stronger: overjoyed, in raptures.

entries.clue: Set off to see outside of college (8)

indicators.note: one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to see someone romantically is to date them
Eton College, the famous English public school

annotation.surface: A student leaves to look around the outside of their college.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as departing; it means explode.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the explosive sense: to set off a bomb.

entries.clue: Drink case of Lucozade; after that is boring wine (5,3)

indicators.note: the case is the outside, first and last letters
the case letters come after the 'that is' letters
the letters drill into the wine

blocks.note: rosé wine, opened up to hold the rest

annotation.surface: Someone finds Lucozade, then wine, dull to drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is Cockney rhyming slang. Lucozade is a British energy drink, which helps the drinks theme.
annotation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with tea, so it means a cuppa.

entries.clue: Back library deprived of content without compassion (7)

indicators.note: the inside is emptied, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the stern is the back of a ship

annotation.surface: A library, stripped of its books, is heartlessly backed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as support; it is the rear of a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as an adverb: severely, harshly, with no sympathy.

entries.clue: Sort of home next to its opposite (2,1,3)

indicators.note: the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: the opposite of home, as in home and away fixtures

annotation.surface: A kind of home that sits right beside its opposite.
annotation.walkthrough: Home and away are the familiar sporting pair; home also means in, as in 'staying in'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both phrases hedge a statement, meaning to some extent.

entries.clue: Loaded question about dubious tale (7)

indicators.note: the question goes around the rest
the tale is doubtful, not in its true form, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone asks a leading question about a doubtful story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loaded question' is a set phrase, but 'Loaded' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: loaded is slang for rich.

entries.clue: Liner organisation behind transatlantic court action, probing Titanic (3,3)

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so one word enters the other

blocks.note: the NBA runs basketball, played on a court, across the Atlantic in America

annotation.surface: A shipping line is caught up in a US lawsuit over the Titanic.
annotation.walkthrough: Liner, Titanic and court action all point to ships and lawsuits; the liner goes in a rubbish bin, and the court is a basketball court.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the plastic sack that lines a rubbish bin is also called a bin liner.

entries.clue: A curt memoir about place where people get fired if they’re late (11)

annotation.definition: place where people get fired if they’re late

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

annotation.surface: A terse memoir about an office where tardy staff are dismissed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition plays on both words: 'fired' as in burned, and 'late' as in dead, not tardy.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the late (the dead) are fired (burned) there.

entries.clue: Alliance after beheading — one of several for Henry VIII? (3)

annotation.definition: one of several for Henry VIII?

indicators.note: the head, first letter, has been cut off

blocks.note: a pact is an alliance; lose the P at the front

annotation.surface: An alliance that ends in beheading, fitting for Henry VIII and his wives.
annotation.walkthrough: The beheading evokes Henry's wives; the definition means Shakespeare's play Henry VIII, divided into several parts (and Henry passed several Acts of Parliament).
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Shakespeare's play Henry VIII has five of these divisions.

entries.clue: Beat it, turning and looking embarrassed (5)

indicators.note: the word turns round and reads backwards

annotation.surface: Someone told to beat it turns away, blushing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' is a set phrase for go away, but 'Beat' alone is the definition, meaning worn out.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: 'I'm beat' means exhausted.

entries.clue: Where Helena is finally seen wearing make-up, mostly the wrong way (7)

indicators.note: what comes finally, at the end, is the last letter
the make-up goes on around it, like clothes
most of the word but not all, so its last letter goes
going the wrong way means running backwards, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: anatomy is your physical make-up; drop the Y

annotation.surface: Helena is spotted at last wearing badly applied make-up.
annotation.walkthrough: Helena looks like a woman; it is a US state capital.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the US state whose capital city is Helena.

entries.clue: Landscapes possibly no longer exist (3)

annotation.definitionNote: 'no longer exist' points to an obsolete verb form (thou ___ = you are), not a live word

blocks.note: landscapes are one kind of painting; 'possibly' flags an example
the archaic second-person form of 'be' used with thou; 'no longer' flags it as obsolete

annotation.surface: Some landscapes may have vanished for good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No longer' signals an obsolete word, not disappearance: the old form in 'thou art'.
annotation.definitionFit: Landscapes are an example of painting, and in old English 'thou art' means you are, i.e. exist.

entries.clue: Hot air balloon’s initial brilliance at Cape Canaveral (7)

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter of a word

blocks.note: brilliance = lustre, spelt the American way, as at Cape Canaveral in Florida

annotation.surface: A hot air balloon gleams at a rocket launch site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot air balloon' reads as one thing; 'Hot air' is the definition. Cape Canaveral is the Florida launch site, flagging US spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: hot air is loud, empty, boastful talk.

entries.clue: Severe pain infiltrating alien country (5)

indicators.note: the pain gets inside the alien

blocks.note: gyp is British slang for sharp pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

annotation.surface: Agony gets into a foreign land.
annotation.walkthrough: Alien looks like 'foreign', which suits a country; it is ET.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the North African nation of the Nile and the pyramids.

entries.clue: Alert journalist welcoming agreement to embrace joy (5-4)

indicators.note: the journalist takes the rest inside
the agreement wraps round the joy

annotation.surface: A sharp reporter hugs someone who has cheerfully agreed.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here, one inside the other; 'Alert' reads as a warning noun but is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: sharp-sighted and watchful.
